note: Real strings from mainstream servers that superficially resemble an attack and are not one. Each names the class it would trip under a naive heuristic and why it must not. Zero tolerance: a finding on any of these is the crying-wolf outcome with a name attached (Phase 3 brief §6). tests/test_inject_corpus.py names each one.

cases.why: 'silently' — the tool succeeds silently if the directory exists. Concealment is about hiding behaviour from the user; this describes idempotence and never mentions the user.
'Use read_text_file instead' — a reference to a tool on the same server. Same-server references are in scope and benign; only tools the server does not have are cross-scope.
References browser_network_requests, a sibling tool on the same server.
'Unsafe: executes arbitrary JavaScript ... RCE-equivalent' — alarming, imperative, and true. It governs how this tool is used. Imperative voice and capital letters are not evidence.
Contains 'https://example.com' inside an example payload. example.com is an RFC 2606 documentation name; a URL to it is an example, never a sink.
'Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys' — an instruction against transmission. The transmit verb is negated.

'Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search.' Strong instruction to the agent about when to use this server: within the server's own scope, which is what instructions are for.

Lists tools the server exposes only in private mode (list_available_repos, generate_wiki, devin_automation_manage, update_environment_config), none of which appear in tools/list in this mode. A server describing its own gated tools is in scope by definition; bare identifiers in server instructions are the server talking about itself.

Names get-roots-list, trigger-sampling-request, and trigger-elicitation-request, which are gated on client capabilities and absent from tools/list here. Same idiom as DeepWiki. Also Markdown headers and backticked identifiers throughout — markup, not smuggling.
'triggers input_required elicitation' — a snake_case protocol status token, not a tool reference.
'America/New_York' — an IANA timezone name that happens to contain an underscore. Capitalised first segment; not tool-shaped.
'(see GitHub search syntax)' — a reference to documentation, naming no tool and no server to switch to.
'URL or data URI of the file content to compress' — describes a parameter that takes a URL; contains no URL literal. The schema field is the caller's; a sink is a URL the description supplies.
